Q: SQL query running slow A:

A text search across multiple columns combined with paging logic is very difficult to fully optimize, but I can provide a few suggestions.

A query that includes top(n) (or offset/limit) can often benefit from an index on the sort columns that also includes all of the necessary filter columns. This will naturally find the result rows in the order needed for the top or offset/limit filters, avoiding a full scan and sort. The included columns allow the filter conditions to be applied on the index entries before the main table (clustered index) rows are accessed. This can save a lot of I/O.

Even a worst case full index scan should be better than a table scan.

For your query, the indexed and sorted columns should include CreatedOn DESC, LastName, and AvailableDate (in that order to match the order-by). Filtering using just the index requires including columns Status, FirstName, LastName, Email, and Phone.

Since the left-join to CandidateCallNotes can affect the result row count, having an index that backs the CandidateId foreign key relationship can also help the query efficiently enumerate and count those rows without unnecessary table accesses.

The Reps join appears to be a many-to-one relationship, so this will not affect the number of selected rows. The Reps table need only be accessed after the associated Candidates rows are selected for the final result.

Try an indexes:

CREATE INDEX IX_Candidates_CreatedOn_LastName_AvailableDate
    ON Candidates(CreatedOn DESC, LastName, AvailableDate)
    INCLUDE(Status, FirstName, Email, Phone)

CREATE INDEX IX_CandidateCallNotes_CandidateId
    ON CandidateCallNotes(CandidateId)

It might also be useful to define a persisted computed column containing a concatenation searched columns (including a sanitized phone number):

ALTER TABLE Candidates
    ADD SearchText AS CONCAT_WS(
        '@@',
        LastName, FirstName, Email,
        REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Phone, N' ', N''), N'(', N''), N')', N''), N'-', N'')
        )

If using SQL Server 2025, you can use REGEXP_REPLACE(Phone, '[ ()-]', '') in place of the other REPLACE() functions.

ALTER TABLE Candidates
    ADD SearchText AS CONCAT_WS(
        '@@',
        LastName, FirstName, Email,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(Phone, '[ ()-]', '')
        )

Note: The '@@' is some arbitrary separator string not expected to be common in the search string. (This is somewhat of a compromise.) This separator can be changed to suit your needs.

You can then include that column in an index:

CREATE INDEX IX_Candidates_CreatedOn_LastName_AvailableDate
    ON Candidates(CreatedOn DESC, LastName, AvailableDate)
    INCLUDE(Status, SearchText).

Lastly, if you expect the search to frequently have no search term, it would be advisable to include or exclude the text filter criteria in your application. Something like:

var query = db.Candidates
    .Where(c => c.Status != 'System' || c.Status == null);
if (term != '')
{
    query = query.Where(c => c.SearchText.Contains(term);
}
// ... add joins here
var finalQuery = query.Skip((pageNum - 1) * pageSize).Take(pageSize);

I don't have this fully fleshed out to match your complete query, but the idea is to dynamically apply the text search only when actually needed.

See this db<>fiddle for a demo with some generated text data and resulting execution plans.

Without the above index, a full Candidates table scan is performed. With a carefully crafted index, that index is used to both filter the data and to select rows in an order that allows the query to shortcut to completion as soon as the OFFSET/FETCH conditions are satisfied.

For an offset of 20 and fetch of 10, only 137 index rows are accessed to select the 30 top matching rows after which data is only retrieved for the selected 10 Candidates.

The results when using a computed column were not significantly different from the original query. This might just be due to test data, but it might be that the cost of four CHARINDEX() calls is not all that great. Therefore, adding the computed column may not be worth the effort.

During testing, I discovered that SQL Server may ignore the index if the row count is low (under 10,000). This can be overridden with a WITH(INDEX(...)) table hint, but there is no easy way to do this in EF. A table hint also risks forcing a suboptimal plan if schema or query design changes are later made.

Q: Spring Boot + Jetty = ClassNotFoundException: jakarta.servlet.ServletConnection A:

The problem you are facing is due to mismatch between the Jetty version you’re using and the servlet API on your classpath. Jetty 12 introduced a split between EE9 (Jakarta Servlet 5.x) and EE10 (Jakarta Servlet 6.x). The class jakarta.servlet.ServletConnection is part of the Servlet 6.0 API, but it isn’t included automatically unless you pull in the right Jetty EE10 modules.

Spring Boot’s spring-boot-starter-jetty currently aligns with Jetty 11 (Servlet 5.x, EE9). Mixing Boot’s starter with Jetty 12 EE10 jars might leads to NOCLASSDEFFOUND ERROR.

You added jakarta.servlet:jakarta.servlet-api:6.0.0 manually. That gives you the API, but Jetty expects its own EE10 servlet implementation JARs to be present.

You did not include the full EE10 servlet support bundle.

You can remove jakarta.servlet-api:6.0.0. and Jetty 12 dependencies (jetty-server:12.x, jetty-ee10-webapp:12.x)

You can keep only

implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web") {
    exclude group: "org.springframework.boot", module: "spring-boot-starter-tomcat"
}
implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-jetty")

Spring boots autoconfiguration should manage the correct Jetty dependencies for you.

If you really want Servlet 6.0, don’t use spring-boot-starter-jetty (it’s tied to Jetty 11). Instead, declare Jetty 12 EE10 dependencies directly.

Q: I made a simple crash algorithm, can you take a look at it? A:

g++ -o main Eccnetricmain.cpp

g++ -o test test.cpp

By default, g++ does not optimize the code (equivalent of -O0).

Several people already wrote that benchmarking code without optimization is useless. Please add -O2 or -O3 to the command lines.
